## Task (taken from Brightspace directly)

Create a short document, with the names of all participating group members. Only one submission per group is required.

You should briefly describe your collaboration tool(s) you’ll use as a group, including for communication, code sharing, and project documentation. You should have identified your data sources, where the data can be found, and how to load it. And you should have created at least a logical model for your normalized database, and produced an Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram documenting your database design.

This is a group project to be completed collaboratively by your entire project team. The goal is to practice effective virtual teamwork, a core professional skill for data scientists.

Note: You are required to deliver an approach document the week before the project code base is due, and make a group presentation at the first meetup after the project code base is due.

Using data, investigate the question:

Which data science skills are most valued?

Treat this as an exploratory analysis. There is no single “correct” answer; your evaluation and justification matter more than any specific ranking.

Project Requirements and Grading Criteria Your group is responsible for the following:

Collaboration

Select and use appropriate tools for collaboration (e.g., version control, shared documentation, task tracking).

Maintain shared access to code, documentation, and findings.

Data Acquisition

Identify relevant data sources. Explain why you chose your data sources.

Explain how the data were collected and loaded.

Store the data in a relational database using a set of normalized tables.

Data Preparation and Exploration

Perform all data tidying, transformations, and exploratory data analysis in R.

Address data quality issues such as missing values and outliers.

Deliverables

Submit all code, results, and documentation.

Clearly document your motivation, approach, and findings.

Presentation

Appoint at least two group members to lead different parts of the presentation.

All students must be prepared to explain how the data were collected, loaded, transformed, tidied, and examined for issue such as outliers.

Statistical Modeling

You are encouraged to experiment with statistical analysis or modeling.

Statistical modeling will not affect your grade, as this is a first-semester course focused on data acquisition and management.

Individual students are not required to explain advanced modeling techniques during the presentation.

To Consider

Did your team define operational proxies for “skill demand” (e.g., job postings, surveys, curricula).

Are there comparisons to make across data sources or longitudinally (across time)?

Attendance and Participation

If you cannot attend the meetup presentation:

Present one-on-one with the instructor before the meetup, or

Submit a 3–7 minute video explaining your work.

Students are strongly encouraged to start early, ask questions, and actively participate in the discussion forum.

Students who are unable or unwilling to work in groups may choose to make Project 3 the one course project that they drop without penalty. There is not an option to deliver Project 3 as a sole contributor.

## Outline

Collaboration tools - zoom (communication) - slack (communication) - github (code sharing)

Data Set selected: Job Postings https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/minmaxer/job-postings-with-salaries CVs?, which has data on job postings between October 5th and October 12th, 2026.

We did explore other databases. For instance, there were other sources for CVs (such as https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/suriyaganesh/resume-dataset-structured/data and https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/saugataroyarghya/resume-dataset) but although CVs could be a good proxy, they reflect what people offer, not what employers are looking for. We also explored descriptions about courses and programs on data science (such as https://www.mastersindatascience.org/learning/data-scientist-skills/hard-skills/ and https: //ischool.syracuse.edu/data-science-skills/). However, they reflect what these institutions teach, which is a reasonable proxy. However, the selected dataset is the best option among these alternatives as it clearly shows what companies expect their workers to do and which sills they are expected to have. Additionally we looked at the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics which has data on employment trends, job openings and turnover, and employment projections. These data are available for various years and by sector. However, unlike the selected data set, they do not mention skills, just the types of jobs.

Database: - Logical model for normalized database - Entity-Relationship diagram

Possible Analysis - look at job market - retrospective - how have events effected job market/resumes - Microeconomics trends - geographic variation - what is a valuable skill (by frequency mentioned or salary)

ROLES:

Data Acquisition (Afwan) - Extract skill information from description - pick N keywords and filter for those results - Database Design Data Preparation and Exploration (Group) - Initial data tidying, Exploratory data analysis, and structuring for R - Perform all data tidying, transformations, and exploratory data analysis in R - Address data quality issues such as missing values and outliers Editor (Jocelyn) - Mash together everyone's analysis into final code base - Everyone to make smaller edits on github Presentation (TBD)
